title: Food relief during the Great Famine in Ireland
cause: Repeated potato blight devastated a staple crop while food continued to leave Ireland.
response: Peel bought imported maize for cheap sale; authorities also distributed relief and organized public works.
outcome: Later public works and limited aid failed to relieve the crisis adequately; shifting relief costs onto landowners also encouraged evictions.
difference: The historical crisis involved colonial power and land tenure; a game price movement alone does not establish famine.

title: Egypt's debt settlement and revenue controls
cause: Egypt negotiated a settlement with representatives of English and French bondholders.
response: The decree pledged railway and Alexandria port revenue to privileged bonds and provided for foreign financial supervision.
outcome: The documented arrangement constrained control of revenue. The reporting consul expected improved debt service; this dispatch does not establish that his forecast was realized.
difference: The document is a contemporary diplomatic account, not proof of later success or a neutral assessment of all affected groups.

sources.title: US Office of the Historian — Farman to Fish, December 1876, FRUS document 345

title: Coordinating sanitation under the Public Health Act
cause: The legislation addressed the sanitary condition of towns and populous places in England and Wales.
response: It provided for local management of water supply, sewerage, drainage, and cleansing under general supervision.
outcome: The Act established a legal framework with geographic exceptions. The statute alone does not demonstrate a particular mortality reduction.
difference: Medical treatment funding and sanitation infrastructure address different mechanisms; the game may model only part of this response.

sources.title: The National Archives — Public Health Act 1848, original statute

title: Limits on textile factory working hours
cause: Factory working time became a subject of statutory regulation.
response: The Factory Act reduced maximum daily hours for women and young people working in textile factories.
outcome: The legal limit was ten hours; the source does not establish universal enforcement or a measured improvement in wages or health.
difference: Historical coverage was limited by age, sex, and industry; the game's national policy may apply more broadly.

sources.title: House of Commons Library — Working Time Directive, RP96/106, Annex 2
